strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing elastic inference across heterogeneous hardware with clear practical relevance
Novel insight that progressive capacity expansion (not just depth) is necessary for vision tasks, validated empirically via Table 1
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple ImageNet variants, extensive ablations (Tables 6-7), and strong baselines comparison
Solid technical execution with token recycling mechanism and entropy-based routing that is simple yet effective
Good presentation with clear figures, thorough appendices supporting reproducibility, and plug-in compatibility with vanilla ViTs
Consistent improvements over nested baselines: up to 2.0 p.p. at equal throughput and 2.9 p.p. at equal GMACs
weaknesses: Fundamental limitation on uniformly difficult datasets (Section 4.5): performance gains critically diminish on ImageNet-A where most inputs require second-stage inference, undermining efficiency benefits in harder deployment scenarios

Strict restriction to vanilla ViT architecture limits practical applicability; no evaluation on hierarchical transformers (Swin, MambaVision) which are increasingly prevalent, despite claims they only 'complicate' slicing

Routing mechanism insufficiently justified: Shannon entropy is simple; claim of parity with complex criteria not empirically validated; entropy thresholds appear manually tuned; negative learned α value (-0.19) unexplained
Training efficiency not quantified: Section 3.3 acknowledges computational intensity but provides no concrete overhead measurements—critical practical information is missing
Limited depth scaling: Table 3 shows 3-stage variants yield diminishing returns with high computational cost, suggesting poor scalability for deeper hierarchies
Evaluation scope restricted to ImageNet classification; no transfer tasks, actual hardware latency/memory measurements, or non-ViT architectures tested
Early exit comparison uses mismatched depths (24 vs 12 layers); parameter-count not controlled across all baseline comparisons; sensitivity to DeiT-Tiny initialization unclear

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Elastic inference across heterogeneous hardware is practically important and clearly articulated

Elegant routing mechanism: Using prediction entropy as global-image-level signal avoids expensive MLP-based routers; the argument that token-level routers cannot capture image-level difficulty is well-justified

Comprehensive experimental validation: Comparisons with strong baselines (MatFormer, HydraViT, SortedNet, DynaBERT), robustness on ImageNet variants (V2, Real, R, A, Sketch), extensions to semantic segmentation (ADE20K, Cityscapes), and hierarchical architectures (Swin)

Token Recycling insight: Observation that naive recursive inference plateaus (Table 1) motivates progressive capacity expansion; ablations convincingly show Final-Layer Token Recycling outperforms alternatives
Strong empirical results: Consistent 2.0 p.p. improvements at equal throughput and 2.9 p.p. at equal GMACs across multiple datasets and settings
Excellent visualizations and analysis: Figures 5-7 effectively show entropy-based routing behavior and load distributions; supplementary material thoroughly documents design choices and failure cases
Backbone-compatible design: Enables seamless transfer to downstream tasks without retraining, demonstrating practical applicability
Clear presentation: Well-structured paper with effective diagrams, intuitive explanations, and comprehensive supplementary material
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Individual components (nested networks, entropy-based early stopping, learnable token projection) are well-established; main contribution is combining existing ideas, which feels incremental

Insufficient mechanistic analysis: Paper shows width expansion outperforms depth expansion empirically (Figure 8b) but lacks deeper insight into why this occurs in vision tasks; Table 1 (naive iteration plateau) only shown for DeiT-Tiny

Token Recycling justification gaps: Learned α converges to −0.19 with no conceptual explanation for negative weighting; KV-cache variant (Table 4) dramatically underperforms (75.67% vs 80.05%) without analysis; why learnable projection outperforms padding (Table 5) unexplained

Fairness of baseline comparisons: All baselines use static compute allocation; no comparison against input-adaptive variants of existing methods; 3H→6H configuration appears tuned to ImageNet-1K (Figure 3), generalization unclear

Training cost and overhead not quantified: Appendix I acknowledges higher training costs for nested models but provides no memory/time benchmarks; ~100 training runs mentioned raises selection bias concerns (cherry-picking risk); Token Recycling overhead (projection + entropy computation) magnitude unknown

Hyperparameter sensitivity under-explored: Entropy threshold τ selection strategy at deployment time not discussed; 3H→6H vs 3H→9H vs 3H→12H trade-offs are dataset-dependent without principled selection guidance; loss weighting [0.5, 0.5] not optimized relative to alternatives

Batch inference efficiency concerns: Algorithm 1 shows dynamic batch shrinkage causing potential GPU underutilization; no empirical analysis of latency overhead from dynamic batching; GMACs/throughput measured at batch size 512 may not reflect real-world small-batch performance

Generalization and scalability questions: Most experiments focus on ImageNet-1K domain; Swin extension uses hand-crafted allocation (entire stage 1 + half of stages 2-4) not generalizable to other hierarchical architectures; no results on larger models (ViT-L/H); extreme pruning regimes (1H→2H) unexplored

Overthinking failure mode unaddressed: ~2% of samples correct in round 1 become misclassified in round 2 (Figure 13); attributed to overthinking but no proposed solution (confidence calibration, ensemble voting) provided; erodes practical trust

Incomplete statistical rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing; unclear if 2-2.9 p.p. improvements are statistically significant given training variance; single runs on downstream tasks (segmentation, Swin) without variance quantification
